TITLE: Nemotron 3 Super: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning  
AUTHORS: NVIDIA  
ONE-LINE TAKEAWAY: Nemotron 3 Super achieves up to 2.2× and 7.5× higher inference throughput than GPT-OSS-120B and Qwen3.5-122B, respectively, while achieving comparable accuracy on common benchmarks.  
- Large language models (LLMs) face trade-offs between accuracy, inference cost, and latency.  
- Existing Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures often neglect hardware constraints like memory bandwidth and communication overhead during inference.  
- Uses a hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture with sparse LatentMoE scaling.  
- Incorporates Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) layers for speculative decoding and inference acceleration.  
- Pre-trains in NVFP4 precision with a 2-phase training process on 25 trillion tokens.  
- Employs a periodic hybrid interleaving pattern of Mamba and attention layers.  
- Achieves up to 2.2× higher inference throughput than GPT-OSS-120B.  
- Achieves up to 7.5× higher inference throughput than Qwen3.5-122B.  
- Supports up to 1 million context length.  
- Achieves 94.7% accuracy on HMMT Feb25 (Math) benchmark.  
- Achieves 60.5% accuracy on SWE-Bench (Coding) benchmark.  
- 120 billion total parameters (12 billion active).  
- 25 trillion pre-training tokens.  
- 2.2× inference throughput improvement over GPT-OSS-120B.  
- 7.5× inference throughput improvement over Qwen3.5-122B.  
- Figure 1 shows accuracy and throughput comparisons with GPT-OSS-120B and Qwen3.5-122B, highlighting higher throughput at comparable accuracy.  
- Figure 2 illustrates the layer pattern of Nemotron 3 Super, showing hybrid Mamba-Attention and LatentMoE configuration.  
- Figure 3 compares standard MoE vs. LatentMoE architectures, demonstrating reduced routing and weight loads through latent space projection.
